chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim — from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the man who appoints a man as executor of his will but he dislikes accepting it — Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not abandon him in this state.'

key_terms.وَصِيَّة: bequest or will — a legally binding instruction entrusted to an executor
key_terms.وَصِيّ: executor — the person designated to carry out the terms of a will
key_terms.يَخْذُلْ: to abandon or forsake — leaving someone without support in a time of need

ai.seo_question: Is a named executor of a will allowed to refuse the appointment in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that when a person has been named as an executor (wasi) of someone's will, he must not refuse and abandon the testator in that condition. This hadith addresses the jurisprudential question of whether a named executor may decline the appointment, with the Imam indicating an obligation to accept in order to protect the testator's interests. The ruling reflects the Islamic principle that one must not leave a fellow believer helpless in a state of need, particularly in a matter as sensitive as the care of one's estate and final wishes.
